A conical grain container has a height of $450\,\text{cm}$ and the radius at the bottom of the container is $90\,\text{cm}.$ The container is being emptied so that the distance $h$ from the top of the container to the grain surface increases at a rate of $\frac{25}{3h}\,\text{cm/min}.$ Find the rate at which the volume of the grain is decreasing when the grain level is $180\,\text{cm}.$ Do not round the answer.

The volume of grain is decreasing at a rate of
{{field-1}} ${\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{min}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the dimensions of the container. Let's call $H=450\,\text{cm}$ the height of the conical container, and $R=90\,\text{cm}$ its radius at the bottom. These quantities are fixed and do not change with time.

Now, let's consider the grain level. We call $h$ the distance from the top of the container to the surface of the grain, $r$ the radius of the cone at the grain surface, and $v$ the volume of the empty space in the container. All of these quantities change with time. In particular, we are given

$$
\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}=\frac{25}{3h}\,\text{cm}/\text{min},
$$

which is positive because the distance from the top of the container to the grain surface increases as the level of the grain in the container decreases. 

We want to know $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}$ when the level of the grain is $180\,\text{cm}.$ At this moment, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}h & =H-180 \\  & =450-180 \\  & =270\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to find a relation between $v$ and the variable for which we know the rate of change, which is $h.$ This is given by the formula for the volume of a cone:

$$
v=\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h
$$

Before we differentiate the equation with respect to time, note that $r$ also appears in the formula. So, we need to simplify the formula by writing $r$ in terms of $h.$

Note that the cones formed by the container and the empty space located between the container's top and the grain surface must be similar. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{r}{h} & =\frac{R}{H} \\ \frac{r}{h} & =\frac{90}{450} \\ r & =\frac{h}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the volume formula as

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {(\frac{h}{5})}^{2}h \\ v & =\frac{1}{75}\pi {h}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we have an equation relating $v$ and $h,$ we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}v & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{75}\pi {h}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{25}\pi {h}^{2}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{25}\pi {h}^{2}(\frac{25}{3h}) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{3}\pi h\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the known values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{3}\pi (270) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =90\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{min}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of grain is decreasing at a rate of $90\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{min}.$
